title: Choose the composition for Funding Agreements
question: The visual world is settled (the Proposals page's world: white ground, Somar Sans, funding teal, amber pending, HC red only for overdue). This choice is how the agreements page is composed. The roll dealt these three; lock one, steer it, or re-roll.

options.label: The Collection Waterfall
options.lineage: a treasurer's cash-collection staircase: promised, scheduled, sent, landed, kept
options.thesis: Every dollar a donor promised walks down one staircase — committed, scheduled, sent, received, net after fees — and the page shows exactly where money is stuck.
options.viewport: Header and filters; then per currency a five-step waterfall across the full width — 6.3M committed stepping down to scheduled, sent, received and net, each drop labelled with its reason (unscheduled, overdue, fees). Clicking a step filters the agreements below to the ones whose money is stuck there. Below: each agreement as a row with donor · proposal, its own tranche beads on a time thread (overdue beads in red), received share, next due date, linked projects and accounts.
options.risk: If the five steps read as a bar chart rather than a story, it becomes decoration; each drop must carry its plain-language reason and count.
options.case: Strongest at answering the manager's real question — 'where is our money and what is late?' — in one glance, then drilling into the exact agreements responsible.

regions.label: title · count · search / donor / currency · record agreement
agreement row — tranche beads on a time thread · projects · accounts

options.label: The Agreement Inspector
options.lineage: a mail client / trading blotter: list on one side, the open record on the other
options.thesis: A dense, scannable list of every agreement on the left; the selected agreement opens beside it as a full live ledger — tranches, fees, rates, accounts, proposal and projects — without leaving the page.
options.viewport: Header and a thin portfolio strip (committed / received / pending per currency). Below, a 40/60 split: left, agreements as compact lines with donor, proposal, budget and a received-share meter, overdue ones flagged red; right, the opened agreement — big budget figure, a tranche timeline from first to last payment with today marked, the fees and exchange-rate trail, and its connections (donor, proposal, projects, accounts).
options.risk: The right pane repeats the show page; it must be faster and richer than clicking through, or it is just a slower eye button.
options.case: Best for an officer working through many agreements in one sitting. Weaker at the portfolio-level 'where is the money' picture.

options.label: The Collection Board
options.thesis: Agreements sorted by what they need from you: overdue, due in 30 days, scheduled later, fully received, nothing scheduled — each column carrying its money total.
options.viewport: Header; a row of five column heads each with a count and total per currency (Overdue in red). Beneath, each agreement as a slip in the column of its most urgent tranche: donor · proposal, budget, received bar, next due date, tranche count.
options.risk: Columns squeeze on laptops and stack on phones; with few agreements most columns look empty.
options.case: Most action-oriented — tells the manager who to chase today. Hides the full funding picture of any single agreement behind its slip.
